subject: Access path selection for Catalyst private deployment — stitch plan
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@catalyst.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Access path selection for Catalyst private deployment — stitch plan

Emma,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great context on Catalyst’s compliance and throughput requirements. Per our discussion I wanted to outline three practical options for connecting your VPCs/on-prem infra to a Redwood Private deployment and propose a small “stitch plan” we can run as a PoC: VPC Peering, PrivateLink (interface endpoints), and site-to-site VPN. High level: which to prefer depends on policy (cross-account peering allowed?), sustained throughput, and whether you need least-privilege network isolation for regulated traffic.

Quick summary of each path (short):
- VPC peering: low-latency, high-throughput; simple routing but cross-account peering policy and transitive routing limits may be blockers. No native IAM-based resource-level controls.
- PrivateLink (interface endpoint): strong least-privilege, works across accounts with endpoint policies; easier to audit with endpoint logs; generally slightly higher per-GB egress than peering but better for regulated data.
- Site-to-site VPN: flexible and quick to stand up; useful as backup or for management/control plane; higher latency and operational overhead for key rotation and scaling.

Attached is a lightweight stitch-plan draft (stitch-plan.pdf) and throughput numbers we ran in a lab (throughput-estimates.csv). Proposed PoC flow:
1) Prod-like PrivateLink for inference traffic (pin model, run latency tests)
2) S2S VPN as fallback for admin/control plane and for regions where interface endpoints aren’t available
3) If Catalyst allows cross-account peering for a dedicated interconnect VPC, run a parallel throughput test comparing peering vs PrivateLink for bulk batch workloads.

Can you confirm Catalyst’s stance on cross-account peering and whether you have a preferred public IP block for VPN termination? If you prefer, we can also run a short runbook for a temporary VPN first and then do the PrivateLink PoC.

Next steps I propose: confirm peering policy, share VPN termination IPs, and pick dates for a 2-day perf run (we can do 11/2–11/3).

—Alex
Alex Martinez
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@catalyst.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Catalyst NetOps <netops@catalyst.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access path selection for Catalyst private deployment — stitch plan

Alex —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few constraints from our side that will steer the decision:
1) Cross-account peering is currently disallowed by our security policy (we're in the middle of an org remodel and peering approvals take months).
2) Anything that exposes our subnets to third-party routing (peering) is a non-starter for the PCI scope we're planning to bring on.
3) We can do interface endpoints (PrivateLink) — we've used them with other vendors and like the endpoint policies for limiting access.
4) VPN is acceptable as a temporary measure for the PoC, but operations prefers not to run production inference over a VPN due to expected throughput and MTU/path issues.

VPN termination: we have two public gateway IPs that can be used for the PoC: 52.11.205.14 and 52.11.205.15.

We also asked our compliance team for a short checklist — they will want PrivateLink + endpoint policy + audit logs in CloudTrail if possible. Do you have an example endpoint policy we can share with them?

If PrivateLink meets our audit requirements, we are inclined to proceed with that as the primary pattern and use VPN for the initial perf test.

—Emma
Emma Liu
Head of Cloud Platforms, Catalyst Systems
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@catalyst.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access path selection for Catalyst private deployment — stitch plan

Emma, Alex —

Thanks for the details, Emma. I pulled together a short technical readout based on your constraints and the attached lab runs. TL;DR: PrivateLink + S2S VPN fallback is the pragmatic, low-risk approach here. Peering isn't viable given Catalyst’s current policy. Below are tradeoffs and a small execution plan.

Tradeoffs (concise):
- Security/isolation: PrivateLink wins. Endpoint policies + per-endpoint SGs give the most auditable and least-privilege model.
- Latency & throughput: Peering can be ~5–15% faster for small RTs and cheaper egress in same-provider scenarios; PrivateLink adds ~1–8ms and an extra hop. For inference (short-response chat use-cases) that's acceptable; for sustained high-bandwidth batch tokenization pipelines, peering has advantages.
- Ops complexity: VPN requires key rotation and monitoring; PrivateLink requires endpoint management and route table cleanup but integrates with our control plane.
- Cost: rough estimate from our lab (see throughput-estimates.csv): PrivateLink PoC estimated additional egress cost of ~$0.02–0.05 per GB vs peering baseline for Catalyst’s projected 50TB/mo. Runbook will size this precisely.

Proposed PoC runbook (2 weeks total, high-level):
1) Week 0: policy & security sign-off (Catalyst to confirm)
2) Week 1: VPN PoC (2 days) — sanity latency + throughput tests using vpn endpoints 52.11.205.14/15. (we’ll use our prebuilt perf harness and capture token-level latencies)
3) Week 2: PrivateLink PoC (2 days) — create interface endpoint(s) in Catalyst account, attach endpoint policies, run same harness, capture CloudTrail logs for endpoint actions
4) Comparison + recommendation: finalize stitch plan and decide whether to keep VPN as hot-standby.

Notes and pre-reqs we need from Catalyst:
- VPC IDs and CIDR ranges for any subnets that will accept the endpoints
- IAM/principal for endpoint policy (we can provide a template)
- Contact for VPN handshakes (we’ll coordinate IKE/SAs)

I’m attaching the endpoint policy template and a one-page perf checklist (stitch-plan.pdf). Quick ask: Alex / Karthik — can you run numbers on the batch-throughput scenario specifically (50–100 Gbps sustained estimate) and whether we should recommend a dedicated interconnect lane (Direct Connect/ExpressRoute) later? If that's on the table, cost math shifts in favour of peering/privatelink hybrid.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Emma / team —

Appreciate the quick confirms. Given Catalyst’s policy and compliance ask, let's lock on PrivateLink as the primary production path and run a short VPN perf PoC next week to validate fallbacks. Action items and owners: 

- Catalyst (Emma): confirm VPC IDs + CIDR ranges and assign an IAM principal we can use in the endpoint policy (due: 2026-11-01)
- Redwood (Marissa): share PrivateLink endpoint policy template and CloudTrail log sizing; create perf harness and baseline (due: 2026-11-01) — attached: stitch-plan.pdf & throughput-estimates.csv
- Redwood (Karthik): run batch-throughput projection for 50TB/mo and estimate egress delta and Interconnect breakeven (due: 2026-11-03)
- Schedule: VPN PoC: 2026-11-09 -> 11-10; PrivateLink PoC: 2026-11-16 -> 11-17

If Catalyst wants a second opinion on costs we can also schedule a short session with our pricing analyst. Otherwise I’ll draft a short MAP (mutual action plan) and share it to HubSpot (HS-34567) by COB Friday.

One minor operational note: for PrivateLink we recommend keeping a dedicated endpoint ENI group per availability zone to avoid cross-AZ egress charges where possible — Marissa can share the setup snippet.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Martinez
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
